summary:
We created Space Wanderers, an educational space‑themed comic project consisting of a cover page plus ten comic pages (Pages 1‑10). The comic follows three main characters — two young astronauts and Deice the Robot — on an adventure travelling from Earth to the Moon and learning key space facts before exploring Mars. We also prepared a full 30‑second narration script and AI‑video prompts to turn the comic slides into a short presentation video.
 
The challenge was to make complex astronomy concepts easy to understand for viewers. Instead of plain text, we used colourful comic art, simple dialogue, and fun facts about lunar gravity, craters, Earthrise, moon phases, retro‑reflectors and Mars. The narration script guides the audience through each page smoothly for a presentation‑style video.
 
This project makes space science engaging and memorable. It encourages curiosity about astronomy, teamwork, and exploration. It is perfect for school presentations, helping the group clearly explain their learning in an exciting, visual way.
details:
Project Details (Space Wanderers Comic & Presentation Video)

What it does / How it works

Space Wanderers is an educational comic slideshow presentation. It tells a story of two young astronauts and Deice the Robot travelling from Earth to the Moon, learning space facts, then discovering Mars. When converted into a 30‑second video, it slides through each comic page while a narrated voice‑over explains every astronomy concept clearly to the audience.

Benefit

- Turns difficult space science into simple, fun, easy‑to‑understand facts

- Visual comic art keeps viewers engaged

- Ready‑made narration script for smooth presentation delivery

- Can be displayed as printed pages, slideshow or short video

Intended Impact

To spark curiosity for astronomy among students. It proves learning science can be exciting, while showcasing the team’s teamwork and research skills for school presentations.

Tools & Software Used

- AI Image Generator: To create the colourful comic pages (Cover + Pages 1‑10)

- CapCut / Pika Labs / Runway: Optional software to compile images, add narration, sound effects and export the final 30‑second video

- Mobile Phone: To view, edit and assemble all pages and scripts

- No coding language or special hardware required

Creativity Factor

Instead of a plain written report, the team built a story‑driven comic adventure. Characters, dialogue and bright illustrations make the science feel alive rather than textbook‑style.

Factors Considered by the Team

- Correct space facts (lunar gravity, craters, Earthrise, moon phases, retroreflectors, Mars)

- Suitable language for the target audience

- Timing for the 30‑second presentation

- Removing Page 11 to keep the video flow smooth

- Equal recognition for every group member’s contribution
